author: CC (second instance), on Akien's instruction: put the questions on the artifacts, keep only the order here
relates_to: every open ticket and trouble named below; each one's own filed_edges (or open_questions, for memory-shape) carries its questions. MAP.md build order; notes/2026-08-05-the-validation-sweep-and-the-build-order.json (the ordering rule this obeys); questions/open-the-frontier-projector.json (the thing that would make this file derived instead of written)
text:
THE ONE THING THIS FILE HOLDS IS THE ORDER. Akien, 2026-08-05: 'if you put the open questions on the artifact itself, and just have a list of the artifacts we need to visit, there will be nothing else to maintain. the state then shows ready to build or ready to design or whatever that specific artifact needs.' So every question below lives ON its artifact in `filed_edges` — the chartered open lane (questions/_charter+why.json, ruling 2026-08-01: an edge IS an open question) — and NOT here. This file is a running order and a marker per stop. It goes stale the moment the frontier projector exists, and that is the point.

THE MARKERS. ASK = blocked on a ruling that is Akien's (a bound, a sequencing, a spec change). MEASURE = answerable by looking at what we already have; no ruling needed, and CC should just go look. BUILD = designed, nothing open, pick it up. PROVE = built, waiting on its proof. WATCH = armed and waiting on a count.

THE ORDERING RULE IS HIS, applied verbatim: 'you go back to the start, you validate every single thing along the way... things that appear either small or foundational, get done first if needed. if two foundational issues, the MORE FOUNDATIONAL of them goes first.' And the path: (1) claude, (2) skills and workflow, (3) foundational components, (4) bus services. Troubles ride ahead of new work in the same layer, because a trouble is the live system now.

=== WAVE 0 — FREE, AND THEY CHANGE THE LIST ===
0.1 tickets/ruling-door-supersede-path — MEASURE. Its own falsifier already reads SATISFIED LIVE 2026-08-02 with the sha256 evidence. Either it is built and the cursor is stale, or something remains the falsifier does not cover. Minutes, and it should not be planned around until it is known.
0.2 troubles/a-boat-resting-in-a-dissolved-state-has-no-door-out (corpus half) — MEASURE. Scan every state string for states absent from its class's current vocabulary. LEARNME was dissolved corpus-wide; build_inspector is the one we happened to find. Never been run.

=== WAVE 1 — A GREEN THAT ISN'T. THE MOST FOUNDATIONAL THING ON THE BOARD ===
Two artifacts are the same animal and neither says so: a proof can pass BECAUSE OF the defect. Under Law 9 this outranks everything below it, because every other green on this list is stated in terms of the instrument these two describe.
1.1 troubles/a-stale-fixture-masked-three-reds-in-intents-own-house — ASK. Is 'died at tooth 1' a different verdict from 'failed at tooth 8'?
1.2 troubles/workflow-cursor-unreadable-by-the-chokepoint — ASK. Its standing says two design questions are Akien's and NAMES NEITHER; writing them down is act one. Candidates now filed on it: writer-side vs door-side, and what stops a proof sampling only the conforming cases.
1.3 tickets/green-is-earned-not-assumed — ASK. Law 9's own physics. What does RUNNING mean for a thing with no process, and where does the site plan get the lots nobody has broken ground on?
1.4 tickets/sorted-renders-the-cursor — BUILD, once 1.2 rules. If the door refuses, this ticket nearly vanishes.

=== WAVE 2 — GATES THAT ARE SUPPOSED TO BE PHYSICS AND ARE POLICY ===
2.1 troubles/every-crossing-goes-around-the-clearance-gate — ASK. Mandatory or advisory? 229 records go around it and harbor_master's own falsifier reads as mandatory.
2.2 tickets/a-voyage-names-its-ticket — ASK. Who writes the exemption roster? Same answer should serve 2.1's bootstrap.
2.3 tickets/clearance-leaves-a-trace — BUILD, after 2.1. It is the instrument that would have measured 2.1.
2.4 tickets/state-machine-physics — ASK. How far back does a failure throw you (back-edges by severity), and does the table carry dissolved states? The second unblocks 0.2/2.5.
2.5 troubles/a-boat-resting-in-a-dissolved-state-has-no-door-out (the act) — ASK. Is there a SCRUB — a re-render that is not a transition? We have already performed it on five tickets and defended it in writing; it is unnamed, not absent.

=== WAVE 3 — THE STORES' OWN DOORS ===
3.1 troubles/notes-store-template-gate-is-prose-not-physics — ASK. Gate wrong or template wrong; and if the gate is right, what happens to the 22 records already on disk (Law 7 forbids quietly rewriting them).
3.2 tickets/the-slate-door-has-a-side-path — ASK, small. Does the generic CLI learn about composing doors, or does a skill declare itself? House pattern says the latter.
3.3 tickets/nothing-rides-loose — ASK. Its falsifier reds on refusing AND on silently absorbing, which leaves a third behaviour nobody has designed. Plus: two roots, one act, what if half fails.

=== WAVE 4 — THE SKILLS BECOME LEARNING BLOCKS (dogfooding the daily instrument) ===
4.1 tickets/skills-migrate-one-blow — ASK. Scope ORDER, not shape: 1.4 and 3.2 are edits to skills inside the same roster of 9, so either they land first or the migration absorbs them. Second: what tooth proves the migration complete, given a hand-listed roster is a tenth thing to maintain.
4.2 tickets/sail-pins-its-refusals — MEASURE then ASK. Where the line sits between structure and phrasing IS the build; three candidates are filed on it.
4.3 tickets/learning-as-a-pattern — ASK. What makes 'it doesn't learn, because X' a valid answer rather than a field everyone fills with N/A.
4.4 tickets/cc-learning-store — BUILD.
4.5 tickets/ticket-and-task — ASK. Where does a task berth? Its own child says it waits on this and it is why the stone has sat.
4.6 tickets/demo-gate — ASK, small. Who binds it, and to what? Unbound, it never fires — the vacuous gate.
4.7 tickets/plan-inspector — BUILD. Reads the plan and reds the disagreements; kin to this very file.
4.8 tickets/stage-needs — BUILD. Two questions filed on it (who may mark, does a mark expire) are deferrable while there is one worker.
4.9 tickets/learning-block-engine-track — ASK. What is the second block? The wrong-intent tell cannot fire until one exists.
4.10 tickets/chart — ASK. The largest surface on the board; six edges already filed on it from its own casting.

=== WAVE 5 — THE SPINE THAT HAS NEVER RUN ===
5.1 tickets/ground-loop-is-discoverable-without-scanning (+ its three THINKME children) — ASK. One number gates all four: the staleness window. A child already assumes 5s and nothing says where it came from.
5.2 tickets/a-record-reaches-disk — MEASURE. What is the first writer? Probably 5.1's liveness record, in which case these are one build and not two.
5.3 tickets/logger-for-bash — PROVE, then WATCH(retention-window).
5.4 tickets/superclaude-starts-itself — PROVE, then WATCH(reported-but-unfixed-floor).
5.5 tickets/host-seam-installer — MEASURE. How does a host-seam declare applies-to on a BARE machine, before anything is installed?
5.6 tickets/bus-completion — ASK. Verb vocabulary ruled or grown? Same shape as 6.2's kinds; answer together or deliberately apart.
5.7 tickets/quarry-index — BUILD.

=== WAVE 6 — BUS SERVICES ===
6.1 tickets/web-server — PROVE. v0 built; the live-render horizon waits on launcher wiring (5.4).
6.2 tickets/a-pane-declares-its-view — ASK. Is the kind vocabulary really closed, and who adds to it? Plus the real work: active_page() takes no arguments, so threading a cursor touches every device with a page.
6.3 tickets/memory-shape — ASK. The biggest design surface: 16 open questions on the artifact, three of them Akien's (THE BOUND; HOW FAST A WEIGHT FALLS; the calving name). Two were answered 2026-08-05 and one ruling was superseded; the build order (embedding layer, then weights, then lexical) is ratified and NOT YET CAST.
6.4 tickets/the-deposit-rides-the-read — WATCH(deposit-drain).

=== NOT TICKETS, AND ONE OF THEM IS FREE ===
I1 intentions-not-beside-code/I-prebuild-cognition-compiles.md — ASK. State reads PROPOSED, awaiting Akien's ratification at the signature gate. It has sat since 2026-07-19 and it supersedes MAP.md:484-505 on ratification. Costs him a yes or a no.
Q6 MAP.md Q6 — ASK. The intention envelope schema. Every intention file in the tree says 'migrates into the intention envelope when that schema lands' — so this one unanswered question is holding a migration named in at least five artifacts.
Q3 MAP.md Q3 — MEASURE. What of UU's memory index crosses over. Overlaps tickets/quarry-index (5.7); doing 5.7 may answer it for free.
Q4 MAP.md Q4 — ASK. Device introspection protocol shape. Overlaps 5.6 and 6.2; three artifacts asking one question.

=== THE MOVE THAT RETIRES THIS FILE ===
questions/open-the-frontier-projector.json is the lane's own first member and it is exactly Akien's instinct made mechanical: nothing today COMPILES every artifact's filed_edges into one frontier view, which is why an ordering had to be written by hand at all. Once it exists, the questions stay on the artifacts (they already do, as of today) and the VIEW derives — leaving only the ORDER as a human judgment, which is the irreducible part. Worth taking early for that reason and not late: it is small, it is a read-only gather over files we already have, and it makes every wave above self-reporting instead of surveyed.

WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT CLAIM. The waves are CC's reading of Akien's ordering rule, not his ruling; the rule is his and the application is a hypothesis under Law 3. Markers are a snapshot of 2026-08-05 and are read off each artifact's own cursor plus its filed_edges — where the two disagree, the artifact wins, and 0.1 is on this list precisely because one of them does disagree. Nothing here is a state: no artifact's cursor was moved to produce it.

=== REVISED 2026-08-05 EVENING — four rulings changed this order, and wave 0 ran ===
The clearance ruling (decisions/2026-08-05-gates-issue-clearances) reaches six stops above. Read this section as the amendment; the waves themselves are unchanged where not named here.

WAVE 0 IS DONE, AND IT MOVED TWO THINGS AND FOUND A THIRD.
0.1 ruling-door-supersede-path — ANSWERED. It is BUILT: supersede at cairn/machines/ruling/ruling.py:303, _cmd_supersede at cli.py:98, four proofs, 2 rulings already retired in anger. The cursor is stale. It now wants ONE ACT, a crossing, which is not CC's to make. Cheapest close on the board.
0.2 the dissolved-state scan — ANSWERED, and the scope is EXACTLY ONE BOAT: build_inspector (to=LEARNME). All 82 tickets parse clean; eight other components only mention a dead token in prose. Under the clearance ruling this may need no fix at all.
0.3 NOT SENT FOR, FOUND ANYWAY: state.json cursors carry SIXTEEN DISTINCT SHAPES across 27 components, against a charter that says state.json is compiled and never hand-edited. This is the empirical case for clearances and it belongs to 2.4.

WHAT THE CLEARANCE RULING DOES TO THE WAVES.
1.2 workflow-cursor trouble — LARGELY DISSOLVES. Its writer-vs-door question answers itself (neither; the writer stops existing). ITS SECOND QUESTION SURVIVES INTACT and is now the whole residue: a proof that samples only the conforming cases passes BECAUSE OF the defect. Same animal as 1.1. ANSWER THEM AS ONE.
1.4 sorted-renders-the-cursor — RETIRED IN PRINCIPLE. Do not build it. Retiring it is a crossing.
2.4 state-machine-physics — PROMOTED, and it is now the biggest lever in waves 1-5. Its back-edge question is retired by 'graph definitely'; its premise is replaced by the clearance design; the build is smaller than the ruling sounds because history.json is already an append-only gate-stamped trail lacking only an owner on its door.
2.5 a-boat-resting — likely dissolves with 2.4. Confirm before building a scrub.
2.1 / 2.3 clearance mandatory-or-advisory and clearance-leaves-a-trace — SUBSUMED into 2.4. Under the ruling a crossing without a clearance did not happen, so 'mandatory' is not a policy choice any more, and the trace is the mechanism rather than an addition to it.

AND ONE NEW STOP, WHICH IS A SECOND CUSTOMER FOR AN INSTRUMENT ALREADY OWED.
N1 THE IMPORT-SCAN — ASK/BUILD. Ruling 2026-08-05-an-inspector-may-not-depend-on-what-it-inspects needs physics, not prose: diagnostic_inspector must import nothing from the shared inspection library, and a sieve reds if one ever appears. CLAUDE.md already owes an import-scan ticket for the db/inference chokepoints; this is its second customer, so one build serves both. It ranks with wave 1, because what it protects is an alarm — and an unguarded alarm is only discovered broken on the day it was needed.
N2 THE SIEVE RENAME — BUILD, timing-constrained. Before or after nothing-rides-loose (3.3), never during.

FOUR RULINGS ARE OPEN AND UNCONFIRMED AT THE DOOR: gates-issue-clearances, a-check-is-worth-its-mesh, an-inspector-may-not-depend-on-what-it-inspects, filters-become-sieves. Each one's what_conforms is a to-do list that stays red until the work lands, and each waits on one act of Akien's: `cairn ruling confirm <id> "<his words>"`. That confirm is the true head of this order — three of the four stops above are unbuildable until it happens, and the hook prints them every turn until it does.
